newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London stocks storm 5,000-point peak, stg weak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London stocks storm 5,000-point peak, stg weak.

text.p: London stocks stormed to a record close on Wednesday as a weak pound boosted prospects for exports and pushed the FTSE index up ...percent past the 5,000-point milestone.

The dollar, meanwhile, slipped slightly against the mark when investors pocketed profits after the U.S. currency hit its highest level in eight years. The dollar's strength was been fuelled by a growing convcition that the Bundesbank has only limited scope to increase interest rates to defend the mark.

Attention was focused on London, Europe's biggest bourse, for much of the day. Shares raced ahead to close up ..... at a record of .... because of strong company results and the sharp drop in sterling.

"Sterling has turned around against the mark and that has given a lift to everything," said the head of equity trading at one top investment bank. "But volumes aren't high and the market feels very 'summery'."
The pound, which has gained weight in recent weeks on hopes of higher interest rates, dropped four pfennigs against the mark on Wednesday as the mood suddenly turned chilly.

A belief that the rates would be increased to contain inflationary pressures gave way to a suspicion in currency markets that the Bank of England, would not sanction a further rise because of complaints from exporters badly hit by the pound's strength.
As investors awaited the outcome of a two-day meeting of Bank of
England policy-makers, which ends on Thursday, the pound was holding on just above 3.00 marks in late Europoean trade. It was also down to $1.60.
"People feel that the chances that rates will be raised tomorrow have distinctly receded," he said. "That has pressed sterling, which in turn is helping the big exporters."

Companies which export or which earn large revenues overseas benefited from the weaker pound. Chemicals group ICI was among the beneficiaries, up 19p at 10.47 sterling. Overseas earners such as TI, BOC and Siebe also advanced.
Oil shares also joined in the rally as investors bet on bumper profits from Shell tomorrow after British Petroleum reported strong profits yesterday.
"It's not just (the oil sector) ... profits have been ahead of expectations almost all the way down the line," said one dealer. An unsettled opening on Wall Street failed to dent London's enthusiasm.
But some dealers said they had been taken aback by the London markets's strength. "I feel uncomfortable with the market at these levels," said one. "The problem is predicting when it will peak."
Stocks in the rest of Europe made healthy gains. Paris was up by nearly 1.6 percent in early afternoon in line with increases in the futures market.
"I'm rather surprised by the rise because I'm pessimistic about the market," said a broker.

In Frankfurt, floor traded ended up 0.8 percent. After-hours trading on the computerised IBIS index made gains of 0.6 percent but traders said uncertainty about the Bundesbank's rates strategy was undermining the market.
Elsewhere in currencies, the dollar edged down by a pfennig as investors took profits after the U.S. currency hit its highest levels since October 1989. It was at 1.8775 marks near the end of trade.

The dollar's latest rally had been fuelled by Wednesday's German unemployment figures which showed a higher-than-expected increase of 17,000 in July, fanning sentiment that the economic recovery was too fragile to allow the Bundesbank to raise rates too far.

In addition, the central bank made a large injection of funds into the German money market on Wednesday in what dealers interpreted as a sign it did not want to raise short-term interest rates for the time being.

"The bottom line is that the Bundesbank's hands are tied," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN Amro. "It has threatened higher rates and if it fails to follow through, it will be the green light for fresh gains. Dollar/mark looks like it could be trading at 1.90 next week."

The Bundesbank has encouraged speculation that it will engineer higher money-market rates if mark weakness persists but this has failed to deter dollar bulls, who say the central bank cannot raise rates high enough to defend the mark in the face of economic fragility.
"The Bundesbank's barrels are empty in terms of what they can do to defend the currency," said Paul Lambert, senior currency strategist at UBS Ltd in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8775 marks and 119.12 yen, compared to 1.8790 and 119.06 in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 56.9 points at 5,017.5.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended up 32.71 points at 4,335.39 in bourse trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 43.43 points at 3027.53.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $319.35 an ounce, compared to $319.85 at the close on Tuesday. Silver was six points lower at $4.34.
